## Summary

Jeffrey Hirsch presents seasonal market rules, including the midterm cycle, winter strength, January signals and sector windows. Eisman accepts parts of the framework while asking for causal explanations. The audit preserves the guest's explicit warnings about unstable signals, small Bitcoin samples and combining disciplines. Statistical claims remain unresolved without the original tests. Eisman's supporting assertions about a universal mutual-fund cash ceiling and nearly all credit growth occurring outside banks are contradicted by primary filings and Fed tables.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

- [H.8 bank balance sheets December 18 2009](https://www.federalreserve.gov/RELEASES/h8/20091218/h8.pdf) (2009-12-18): Historical H.8 tables record trillions in bank loans, including large commercial, real-estate and consumer portfolios; these are comparable categories for testing claims of zero subsequent bank loan growth. PDF text inspected; screenshot retrieval failed.
- [H.8 bank balance sheets November 6 2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h8/20261106/) (2026-11-06): All-commercial-bank loans and leases exceed $14 trillion, with commercial and industrial loans near $3 trillion and real-estate loans about $5.9 trillion. Banks have contributed substantial post-crisis credit growth, though categories and reporting conventions require adjustments for exact growth shares.

## Framework and tools

- Distinguish executable fixed-window strategies from ex-post low-to-high returns.
- Compare conditional success rates with the market's unconditional upward bias.
- Retire failed signals and preserve out-of-sample tests.
- Combine seasonality with fundamentals, technicals, policy and sentiment.
- Do not turn a historical average into a dated target.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Midterm-to-pre-election return tables.
- Best-six-month switching strategy and MACD.
- Intraday and payroll-linked flows.
- January trifecta and sector seasonality.
- Dow super-boom target.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Jeffrey Hirsch. Most return statistics and all super-boom targets are Hirsch's. Eisman supplies separate flow, Bitcoin, payments and private-credit views.
- Full transcript read in two contiguous parts, advertisements and ending included.
- Guest is Jeffrey Hirsch; captions abbreviate surname inconsistently.
- A confused passage says the Dow is already past 62,000 then immediately places it near 45,000; preserve the explicit future 2030 target rather than score that apparent transcription slip.
- Closing recap compresses the midterm horizon differently; main interview supplies the more precise Q4-to-Q2 window.
